steel_spread.note: US EAF metal spread equals HRC minus prime busheling scrap, the margin that drives Nucor and Steel Dynamics. HRC in $/short ton (SMU, published weekly); scrap in $/gross ton (RMDAS, settles monthly). Spread shown in $/short ton with scrap converted at 1 gross ton to 1.12 short tons. Benchmark data on weekly/monthly cadence, not a live tick. Update HRC weekly and scrap monthly from the cited sources.

NUE.name: Nucor Corporation
NUE.briefing:
### Nucor (NUE): trader read

The bellwether. Largest US steelmaker at roughly 25 to 30 percent of domestic capacity, all electric arc furnace, so the cost base flexes with scrap instead of sitting in fixed blast furnace overhead. Nucor sets the HRC spot price the rest of the market follows.

The swing factor is the metal spread: HRC selling price minus busheling scrap. When it widens, Nucor prints. Diversified across sheet, bar, structural and plate, which smooths the cycle versus a pure flat rolled name.

**Watch:** scrap costs, non residential construction, tariff headlines.

STLD.name: Steel Dynamics, Inc.
STLD.briefing:
### Steel Dynamics (STLD): trader read

The growth EAF. Number three US carbon steel producer, same scrap fed model as Nucor with a lower cost reputation. The Sinton, Texas mill is the story: as it ramps it adds flat roll supply into the South and lifts volumes.

Vertically integrated into scrap through OmniSource, which hedges the input side. Moves in step with Nucor on the same spread and tariff drivers.

**Watch:** Sinton utilization, the scrap spread, fabrication backlog.

CLF.name: Cleveland-Cliffs Inc.
CLF.briefing:
### Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF): trader read

The high beta integrated play. Largest flat rolled supplier to US autos, running blast furnaces rather than EAFs, so it carries more fixed cost and more operating leverage. It screams higher when steel rallies and hurts when it fades.

Owns its own iron ore, so raw material is internal but capex is heavy. Trades at a cheaper multiple than the EAF names on debt load and thinner diversification.

**Watch:** auto build rates, iron ore, debt maturities, recurring M&A chatter.

AA.name: Alcoa Corporation
AA.briefing:
### Alcoa (AA): trader read

The aluminum pure play, a different animal from the steel names. Vertically integrated from bauxite mining through alumina refining to primary metal, so the P&L tracks the LME aluminum price and alumina spot, with smelter power costs as the real swing factor.

This is not a steel spread story at all. Different commodity, different driver.

**Watch:** LME aluminum, alumina prices, energy contracts, import tariffs.

RYZ.name: Ryerson Holding Corporation (incl. Olympic Steel)
RYZ.briefing:
### Ryerson plus Olympic Steel (RYZ): trader read

The distributor, not a producer. Buys, processes and resells stainless, aluminum, carbon and alloy, so it earns on spread and volume rather than the direction of any one metal.

The Olympic Steel merger closed early 2026 and lifted revenue more than 30 percent year on year on the combined book. Margins live and die on service center spreads and integration synergies.

**Watch:** service center spreads, synergy delivery, industrial demand. Capacity is not a meaningful metric for a distributor.
